header: Date: Tue Mar 31 2026 08:00 AM PDT | Duration: 45 min | Platform: Zoom | Recording: yes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Evan Liu (Redwood) - Lisa Morales, Jordan Kim, Priya Shah, Marcus Green (Octane Retail)
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost optimization, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Agreed to run a month-long pilot for Dedicated capacity for peak holiday P95s and follow up with technical deep-dive on KV caching and latency tuning.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted for holiday peak
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're conscious of people's time so we'll go through Q1 usage, cost, ops, and then roadmap. Lisa, you want to kick off with any top-of-mind items from Octane?
[00:22] Lisa Morales: Yeah thanks Maya. Quick context — we've rolled Redwood into our recommendation microservice in Jan, been steadily increasing traffic, we're now at about 120 rps steady state and spikes to ~400 during promos, which is where costs kinda jump.
[00:40] Jordan Kim: yep and to add, most of the traffic is short responses but we have a couple longer chat flows for support which hit 512-1024 token windows. The KV cache hit rate is maybe 38% right now, so a lot of repeated prefixes.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Got it. On the Redwood side we've seen the same — prefix cache could be helping a lot there. Ravi can you share the high level on their billing and any surprises?
[01:18] Ravi Patel: Sure; high level, Octane's Q1 spend for inference was $36k raw, embeddings another 6k. Unit cost is trending up during spikes because autoscale pushes into burst nodes without batching benefit. There's also a couple of weighty prompt templates that push token counts.
[01:40] Priya Shah: question — is that more dedicated vs hosted? We're currently on Hosted with a few reserved routes but no Dedicated pools.
[01:50] Evan Liu: Right now you're on Hosted, which gives flexibility but less predictable tail latency during big spikes. Dedicated would let you pin GPUs and ensure you get consistent P95s for your 400 rps spikes. There's also mixer options — like reserved capacity with burst.
[02:10] Lisa Morales: Our main worry is cost for the holiday promo season; we need predictable budgets and P95 under 220 ms for the recommendation path.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Makes sense. Two levers: batching/config tuning + Dedicated for the promo window. We can simulate your spike profile and estimate savings from higher cache hit + batching.
[02:35] Jordan Kim: If we go Dedicated, what are the ops requirements? We have to ensure VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs.
[02:45] Ravi Patel: We support Private/VPC and KMS. For Dedicated, we provide private endpoints and audit logs; there is a short onboarding for VPC peering and KMS ARN. We'll send a checklist.
[03:00] Marcus Green: Any SOC2/ISO evidence? Legal wants to see certs before we scope Dedicated.
[03:06] Maya Chen: Yep we'll attach SOC2 Type II summary and the security whitepaper. Evan, you wanna talk about reliability incidents we logged?
[03:15] Evan Liu: Sure, there were two brief infra incidents in Feb tied to autoscaler cold starts; both were mitigated with fallback routing to a smaller model variant. Latency spikes were 300-600ms for about 2-4 minutes. Since then we've tuned the cold-start profile and raised min replicas during the promo schedule.
[03:40] Priya Shah: did you see any quality delta with the fallback model? Our concern is accuracy drop for rankings.
[03:48] Evan Liu: Good question — we measured a ~2% drop in NDCG on the benchmark prompts during fallback windows. We're recommending policy-based fallback only for non-critical reads, and can set up canaries.
[04:04] Lisa Morales: Okay, that 2% isn't great but might be acceptable if it's short. We need an SLA plan around it.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Agreed. For SLAs we can include an availability target and automatic rollback to baseline model. We'll include fallback policies in the proposal.
[04:20] Jordan Kim: On the technical side, Evan you mentioned KV cache improvement could help — what's realistic?
[04:28] Evan Liu: With current workload patterns I'd expect caching hit to move from 38% to ~62% with prefix-level eviction tuning and increasing cache memory per replica. That plus batching could cut token cost by ~25% on promo spikes. We'll run a perf sim next week.
[04:48] Lisa Morales: Nice. What about quantization? We tested int8 earlier in sandbox, recall we saw some small latency win but some output drift.
[04:58] Evan Liu: Right — quantization can reduce memory / improve throughput but at risk of small quality regressions. For ranking we recommend conservative quant profiles; for candidates we can be more aggressive. We'll include model/quantization recommendations in the follow-up.
[05:14] Priya Shah: For the Dedicated pilot, do you support hybrid routing? Like keep some routes hosted for non-critical dev traffic?
[05:22] Maya Chen: Yes you can route by policy per endpoint — keep dev/dev-test on hosted, prod-critical on Dedicated. We can show your routing config in the console.
[05:32] Marcus Green: A quick question from finance — how would committed reserved pricing look? Any ballpark?
[05:38] Maya Chen: We'll provide a committed capacity estimate based on your spike profile; rough ballpark is 18-25% unit cost reduction over pure hosted at our typical commit levels, plus operational predictability. We'll include precise numbers in the pricing sheet.
[05:55] Lisa Morales: Great. Roadmap alignment — we plan multi-channel promo in Nov, that's when we need Dedicated. Timeline for onboarding?
[06:05] Ravi Patel: Typical Dedicated onboarding from LOI is 4-6 weeks for config and peering, plus any security review. If you want the pilot earlier we can run a 30-day pilot on Dedicated in late Sep for a rehearsal.
[06:20] Jordan Kim: We'd prefer a month-long pilot in Sep, then go full Dedicated by Oct if all good.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. We'll draft a pilot scope — target metrics: P95 under 220ms, cache hit >=60%, cost per 1k requests reduced by 20% during spikes.
[06:40] Lisa Morales: We'll want those metrics captured in the Console and shared as a dashboard.
[06:45] Evan Liu: We'll create a dashboard template and share a Grafana link. Also we'll export the token-level cost breakdown for your finance team.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Security follow-ups — KMS integration, SSO, SCIM?
[07:02] Ravi Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; KMS via customer-managed key (AWS KMS/HSM). We'll include steps and the audit log export format.
[07:14] Marcus Green: Any blockers for on-prem/private deployment? We might consider that for EU data residency.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Private on-prem is doable but a larger lift; VPC/private control plane is faster. For EU residency we have regional private endpoints — we'll surface options.
[07:33] Lisa Morales: Ok let's list immediate next steps.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Recap — Maya will send usage/cost export; Evan to run perf sim and schedule deep-dive; Ravi will share SOC2 and KMS/SSO docs. Octane to confirm pilot dates and provide on-prem footprint if considering private. Any final questions?
[07:52] Priya Shah: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[07:56] Maya Chen: Thanks all, will follow up with notes and items.
[08:00] [meeting ends]
questions: What are cost drivers during promo spikes?
Can Dedicated meet P95 under 220ms for recommendation path?
What security artifacts are needed for Dedicated?
